newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes show continuing signs of strength.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes show continuing signs of strength.

text.p: Trade of North Sea crudes on Monday caught some traders by surprise with premiums holding steady to firmer, traders said.
"I thought we had seen the top of this market but it might not be so. People seem willing to pay up and not just for Brent," one buyer said.
Jan Brent on the IPE futures gained some 41 cents to trade at $23.18 a barrel by 1841 GMT in a late rally led by NYMEX products.
A cargo of Brent loading December 14-16 sold on Monday at Jan Brent +35 cents -- up five cents from deals on Friday.
Two further Brents moved -- both at premiums to dated Brent. A Dec 15-17 loader at +5 cents and Dec 17-19 at Dated +4 cents.
Both Brent cargoes from Monday's paper chains were kept and traders expected Tuesday's two to be taken out before the five o' clock deadline as well.

One million barrels of end December Statfjord was bought by a refiner at a healthy dated Brent +43 cents and, although talk of a December 24-26 Forties moving at the same premium could not be confirmed, traders saw the level as reasonable.
"Margins are good and I don't see that much crude left," one equity holder said.
At least four end month Ekofisk cargoes were still for sale as well as a few Osebergs but supply of Forties and Statfjord was not as plentiful.
The strike at Elf's three French refineries continued into its fifth day saw traders waiting for cargoes to come back on the market.
